clause_verbatim: One anchor drill before the freeze against the real remote on a drill branch and the real issue thread, with a mock chain carrying the real freeze-receipt fields (a throwaway repository could not reveal identifier leaks, because its URLs lack the real account and repository names).
what_changes: The drill's postings go to a dedicated, clearly labelled drill issue in THIS repository (ykzeng-yale/ICLR-WinRatioAgentEval), linked from issue 11, instead of into issue 11 itself.
what_does_not_change: the repository: the real one, so the real account and repository names appear in every URL, which is the stated reason 12.4 item 10 rejects a throwaway repository
the posting count: the finite 20 already planned
the mock chain carrying the real freeze-receipt field shapes
config.json anchor.issue, which remains 11: a TRIAL still anchors to issue 11. This amendment governs the DRILL only.
config.json anchor.posting_latency_p95_s, which remains null and frozen; the drill does not write it
why: Issue 11 is the scientific coordination thread the root session reads every cycle. Twenty drill postings into it would bury coordination under synthetic anchors. A separate issue preserves the real repository and identifier surface -- the purpose of the clause -- without that cost.

authority.verbatim: Proceed with option (b): one clearly labelled dedicated drill issue in this same repository, linked from issue 11, with the already planned finite 20 postings. Record this location-only prefreeze amendment before the first post; retain all attempts, timestamps, failures and usage. No PR. This is explicit authorization for that bounded drill, not silence or permission to start the model study.

what_this_amendment_does_not_authorize: any model call, server start, trial episode or calibration episode
treating the drill's empirical p95 as a guaranteed future worst-case bound
any change to the trial anchoring location
enforcement: experiments/live_ab_tools/anchor_drill.py refuses to post unless this file exists AND is committed with no uncommitted changes.
